newsitem.title: USA: Six tunnel out of Pittsburgh prison.
newsitem.headline: Six tunnel out of Pittsburgh prison.

text.p: Six inmates, two of them convicted murderers, tunneled out of a maximum security prison on Wednesday and escaped, officials said.
"This breakout was a unique occurrence ... we think it was planned for weeks," Greg White, supervisor of Western Penitentiary prison in Pittsburgh, said at a news conference.
White said the six men escaped sometime between 6 a.m. and 10:30 a.m. EST on Wednesday. The men dug a tunnel from inside the prison, but White did not elaborate how they managed to do so.
Terry Hunt, a Pennsylvania State Police officer who was leading the search team, said it was unknown if the men were armed.
"They should be considered dangerous based on their prison records," he said.
A search for the fugitives was under way on the ground and by helicopter.
Hunt said a 1989 bronze-coloured Pontiac Bonneville was reported stolen in the vicinity of the prison after the men were discovered missing.
The fugitives were identified as Tom Berkelbaugh, Andrew Heim, George Conrad, Carmen Keller, Nuno Pontes, and Leslie Billingsley. Conrad and Keller were serving murder sentences.
Western Penitentiary has more than 1,800 inmates.
